newsitem.title: UK: JAPAN FUNDS TURN BEARISH ON PACIFIC BASIN-SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN FUNDS TURN BEARISH ON PACIFIC BASIN-SURVEY.

text.p: Japan-based fund managers are seeking to trim positions in Pacific Basin equity markets, a Merrill Lynch survey said.

"In the wake of recent slides in the smaller Asian markets, bears now outnumber bulls by 43 percent on a three-month view," Merrill said. Sellers outnumber buyers by 17 percent in the August survey, which polled 36 institutions managing $484 billion.
Fund managers in Japan are eager to buy European equities, with buyers outnumbering sellers by 29 percent, the highest figure in three years.
Patchy data in the aftermath of Japan's April sales tax rise is causing Bank of Japan rate hike fears to recede, according to Merrill.
Fund managers expect to see a rise in the discount rate, with 75 percent of respondents expecting a rise in the coming year, against 80 percent last month.
A bullish view on the dollar helped average forecasts for earnings growth in FY 1998 to increase to 9 percent, up from 8.1 percent last month.

"The sales tax increase in April has thrown a smoke screen over the Japanese economy," said Bijal Shah of Merrill Lynch. "When a weak economic report is published it is impossible to tell if it is a temporary reaction to the tax increase, or a sign that the underlying economy has weakened. Until the smoke clears, the market will be driven by investor sentiment."
Buying interest in Japanese stocks continued strong, with bulls outnumbering bears by 46 percent, up from 33 percent last month.
The survey was carried out for Merrill by Gallup between August 4 and 5. -- James Saft, London newsroom +171 542 2734
